description:
Found s395 while ruling out seven apparent coverage decreases (they were
contention artifacts).  MEASURED, so do not re-derive: this is a HANG, not a
slow file.

  tools/run-perl-suite.pl re/regexp.t --jobs 1 --timeout 150   ->  793 ok / 112
  tools/run-perl-suite.pl re/regexp.t --jobs 1 --timeout 400   ->  793 ok / 112
  blessed snapshot (docs/perl-suite-run.tsv)                   ->  793 ok / 112

Nearly 3x the time budget, byte-identical counts.  It stops dead at TAP row 906
(793 + 112).  A slow file would have produced more rows with more time -- and
the contended --all run at 90s produced FEWER (344), which is what slowness
looks like, so both behaviours are visible in the same data.

SIX FILES SHARE IT.  re/regexp.t, regexp_noamp.t, regexp_notrie.t, regexp_qr.t,
regexp_qr_embed.t and regexp_trielist.t are six drivers over ONE data file,
t/re/re_tests (2169 lines, one independent regex test per line), differing only
in flags.  All six read ~793 in the snapshot.  Perl runs 2167 of them.  So the
unmeasured tail is roughly (2167 - 905) x 6 ~= 7500 rows, plus comp/require.t.

WHY IT IS CHEAP TO LOCATE: the driver emits TAP as it goes and each row is an
independent test, so the LAST row emitted names the pattern.  Do NOT add exits
to the .t file (perl's own t/ files are authoritative here and are never
edited) and do NOT bisect by hand:

    cd <perl t/ dir> && timeout 200 <pcl runner> re/regexp.t 2>&1 | tail -3

The last `ok N - ...` line's description carries the pattern; re_tests line
N+1-ish (modulo skipped rows) is the offender.  Confirm by running that one
pattern alone through PCL.

THEN, one of two shapes:
  * catastrophic backtracking in cl-ppcre (the #196 family) -- the pattern
    needs a bounded match, or the file needs the same registration #196's
    other victims get;
  * a genuine infinite loop in PCL's own matching/translation, which is a bug
    with a two-line reproducer.

SEPARATELY (do this regardless, it is the #176 hole): none of these six, nor
comp/require.t, has a row in docs/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv.  A file that TIMEOUTs
contributes NO rows, so its passing rows vanish into a number that reads as a
regression -- which is exactly what cost s395 a re-measure.  comp/require.t is
the SLOW case (909 at --timeout 300, 350 at 90s), so it wants a registry row of
~300s.  re/pat_advanced.t already has one at 900s as the precedent.

BAR: name the offending re_tests line and its pattern; fix or register it with
a cause; re-run all six files and splice their snapshot rows; add the
timeouts.tsv rows for whatever remains genuinely slow.


=== s469bf (2026-09-05, Opus) — re/speed.t's and re/overload.t's counts are a LOAD
=== reading, and the I4 stamp is capable of recording a lucky one ===

Found while attributing the s468 companion ROW DIFF: 34 of the 199 NEW rows were
re/speed.t's, and they are not a regression, a fix, or a volatile key — they are
the clock.

  session   re/speed.t (snapshot: TIMEOUT 1/0)            re/overload.t (snapshot: TIMEOUT 3/0)
  s465az    TIMEOUT 25/30                                 TIMEOUT 0/0
  s466      TIMEOUT 0/0                                   TIMEOUT 0/0
  s468      TIMEOUT 25/19 parallel, DIFF 25/34 serial      TIMEOUT 0/0
  s469bf    TIMEOUT 25/0  parallel, TIMEOUT 25/25 serial   TIMEOUT 0/0

Because s468's #366 serial re-run happened to come back DIFF, the file was
row_verifiable for that run and its 34 diverging rows were reported as NEW ROW
against an empty blessed set.  In s469bf's run of the same tree it stayed
TIMEOUT and the identical rows landed in the "~ N new row(s) in a file that
produced no comparable TAP — noise, not a regression" bucket instead.  Same
tree, same rows, opposite bucket.  NOT BLESSED, deliberately.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both worth knowing before anyone acts on these files:

 1. The s468 SHORTFALL advisory `re/speed.t 4 -> 0 row(s) — fixed; EDIT the
    baseline row` must NOT be acted on.  A TIMEOUT run is skipped by the
    shortfall comparison entirely, so the 0 was only produced because that one
    serial re-run finished; blessing 0 would turn every future completing run
    that reads 55 of 59 rows into "a file lost rows it used to produce: this
    run is NOT clean".  baselines/row-shortfall.tsv keeps `t/re/speed.t 4`.

 2. The I4 stamp (baselines/perl-suite-notrun-stamps.tsv) records the VERDICT
    of the run that stamped it, so s468's row reads `re/speed.t … — measured
    DIFF 25/34`.  That is a true record of that run and a misleading record of
    the file: the very next run of the same tree measured TIMEOUT.  For a
    member of this hang set the stamp answers "when", never "what".

s469bf did not re-stamp these files (the s468 stamps are one day old and its own
`--dir re --dir comp --dir run` run confirms every one of them); re-stamping
would have cost ~30 minutes of hang-file timeouts for a one-day-fresher date.
subject: re/regexp.t and its five siblings HANG at TAP row 906 (~7500 rows unmeasured); comp/require.t is separately just slow
